Transform intensity column by applying a function

Source: R/prolfqua-deprecated.R
transform_work_intensity.Rd

Transform intensity column by applying a function

Usage

transform_work_intensity(pdata, response, .func, .funcname = NULL)

Arguments

pdata

data.frame

response

character, name of the response column to transform

.func

function to transform intensities e.g. log2

.funcname

name of function (used for creating new column name)

Value

list with data (data.frame), colname (new column name) and zeros (logical, rows whose zero intensity became NA)

Details

For log, log2 and log10, zero intensities mean "not detected" and become NA; LFQData records them in its provenance. Negative intensities give NaN with a warning, which fitting and aggregation then reject.

Note

Deprecated in prolfqua 1.9.5; use LFQData$get_Transformer()$intensity_array(). See prolfqua-deprecated.
